technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go for all backend, orderer, and CLI components to align with the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase.
The Solo orderer will utilize an in-memory data structure for the RAM ledger, supporting seek operations for client reconnections.
The standalone CLI will be decoupled from peer internals by relying on gRPC client libraries, removing the RocksDB dependency.
The state cache will implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) caching mechanism to optimize read/write set building.
assumptions: The developer is highly experienced with Hyperledger Fabric architecture and the Go programming language.
Unit and integration testing, along with basic CI/CD pipeline updates, are included within the respective feature activities.
Documentation will be authored in Markdown and integrated into the existing Hyperledger documentation infrastructure.
GitHub repository setup involves mirroring or migrating from Gerrit without losing commit history.

activities.activity_description: Implement the ability for application developers to provide and use a friendly name to identify, manage, and debug chaincode (U1).

activities.activity_name: Lifecycle System Chaincode for Deployment Policies
activities.activity_description: Develop the lifecycle system chaincode (cc) to allow chaincode developers to manage deployment policies for chaincodes (U2).
Write and publish documentation for chaincode upgrade flows and ensure all Hyperledger Fabric documentation is easily accessible at hyperledger.org (U3, U7).

Implement the 'Solo' ordering process with a single orderer, buffered channel for batches/blocks, and a simple in-RAM ledger that allows clients to seek within history for disconnection/reconnection (U4).
Migrate or mirror the Hyperledger Fabric code to GitHub so developers can explore it without Gerrit access (U5).
Implement a state cache to help submitters quickly build the read-write set, leading to better performance (U6).
Extract peer commands into a separate, standalone CLI component that is not dependent on peer node internals (like RocksDB), allowing easy installation as a platform-specific binary (U8).
